info.title: Tron runner protocol
info.description:
How a runner talks to Tron over a WebSocket. This document is generated from the Rust frame types Tron itself serializes and parses, so it cannot describe a frame Tron does not speak.

Compatibility and versions. A runner states the protocol it speaks in `announce.announcement.protocol_version`, a `RunnerProtocolVersion`. This document describes `v1`, the only version, and Tron decodes only the frames and fields defined here: an unknown frame `type`, a missing or extra field, or an unknown `protocol_version` is answered `protocol_error` with reason `malformed_message`. Runners that never announce are legacy sessions and stay compatible for this release. A change a `v1` runner could not handle (a renamed or removed frame, field or reason value, or a new required field) is published under a new `protocol_version`, not made to `v1`, and this document's `x-runner-protocol-version` names the version it describes.

runners.title: Runner WebSocket
runners.description:
Frames are JSON text frames, each an object whose `type` names the frame. A runner authenticates (see the `worker_api_key` scheme), may `announce` its handlers and capacity once, receives `work`, replies at once with `accept`, and finally sends one `report` carrying the one-time secret from `accepted`. A report may arrive on a different connection with the same worker API key than the one that accepted.

Delivery modes decide how deliveries of one run relate. For `one_runner` jobs one delivery per run wins: simultaneous accepts race under the run lock, exactly one gets `accepted` and every other delivery's `accept` is answered `accept_refused` with reason `already_resolved`. For `every_connected`, `advanced_at_most` and `advanced_at_least` jobs several sessions receive a delivery; each delivery is accepted and reported independently, no accept is refused because another runner accepted, and the job's delivery mode decides how many successful outcomes make the run succeed.

Refusals and rejections are closed sets: `accept_refused` carries an `AcceptRefusal`, `report_rejected` a `ReportRejection` and `protocol_error` a `ProtocolViolation`, each published with a description per value. Tron sends no free-text error.

accept.name: accept
accept.title: accept
accept.description:
Takes on a delivery Tron pushed with `work`. Send it straight away,
before the delivery's `accept_deadline`. Tron answers `accepted` or
`accept_refused`.

accept_refused.name: accept_refused
accept_refused.title: accept_refused
accept_refused.description: Answers an `accept` Tron would not take. Do not run the job.

accepted.name: accepted
accepted.title: accepted
accepted.description:
Answers a successful `accept`. Keep the secret: it is shown here
once and never again, and `report` must echo it.

announce.name: announce
announce.title: announce
announce.description:
Optional, at most once per connection, after `authenticated`: declares
what this runner can do. Tron answers `announced`. Runners that never
announce are listed as legacy sessions and still receive work.

announced.name: announced
announced.title: announced
announced.description: Confirms that this connection's `announce` was retained.

authenticate.name: authenticate
authenticate.title: authenticate
authenticate.description:
Must be the first frame on a new connection. Anything else, or no
frame in time, is answered with `authentication_failed` and the
connection is closed.

authenticated.name: authenticated
authenticated.title: authenticated
authenticated.description:
Answers a valid `authenticate`. Several runner processes may
authenticate with the same worker API key at once; each connection
gets its own session.

authentication_failed.name: authentication_failed
authentication_failed.title: authentication_failed
authentication_failed.description:
The first frame was not a valid `authenticate` in time: a timeout, a
malformed or non-text frame, another frame type, or an unknown,
revoked or mismatched token. The connection is closed right after.

protocol_error.name: protocol_error
protocol_error.title: protocol_error
protocol_error.description:
An authenticated runner sent a frame the protocol does not allow. The
connection stays open.

report.name: report
report.title: report
report.description:
The one final result of an accepted delivery. It may be sent on any
connection authenticated with the same worker API key, for example a
new one after the runner restarted. Tron answers `report_recorded` or
`report_rejected`.

report_recorded.name: report_recorded
report_recorded.title: report_recorded
report_recorded.description: Answers a `report` Tron recorded. The delivery is finished.

report_rejected.name: report_rejected
report_rejected.title: report_rejected
report_rejected.description: Answers a `report` Tron could not record.

work.name: work
work.title: work
work.description:
A run has been dispatched to this connection as one delivery. It
carries no job input or payload: only ids, the job's name and times.

receive_runner_frames.title: Frames a runner sends to Tron
receive_runner_frames.description: Every frame a runner may send, defined by `RunnerMessage`.

send_server_frames.title: Frames Tron sends to a runner
send_server_frames.description: Every frame Tron may send, defined by `ServerMessage`.

oneOf.description: No delivery with this id was pushed to this connection's session under an unrevoked worker API key. Accept on the connection that received the `work`.
The delivery's `accept_deadline` had passed, including when it had already been marked failed to deliver.

This same delivery was already accepted (or is in flight) or reported, or its run was cancelled. A cancelled run's delivery stays `pushed`; the accept is refused because the run is cancelled. For `one_runner`, another delivery for this run already won the run-scoped accept race. Broadcast modes do not choose a winner.
A frame was not JSON for any runner frame (an unknown `type`, a missing or extra field, including a handler key that does not match the published handler-key schema), or was a binary frame.
Reserved; not sent today. A first frame other than `authenticate` is answered with `authentication_failed`.
`authenticate` was sent again on an authenticated connection.

The announcement broke a constraint: zero capacity; no, too many, duplicate, blank or oversized handler keys; a blank or oversized display name or runner version; or a blank, oversized or non-semver SDK version.
`announce` was sent twice on one connection. Reconnect to replace the announcement.

ProtocolViolation.description: How an authenticated runner broke the protocol.

oneOf.description: No delivery with this id belongs to the reporting worker API key, or that key is revoked.
The secret does not match the one issued in `accepted`, or the delivery was never accepted, so no secret was issued.
The secret matched, but the delivery already has its one final report.

RunOutcome.description:
The result a runner reports: exactly one of `ok` or `err`, each carrying
a single string, so it serializes as `{"ok": "..."}` or `{"err": "..."}`.

RunnerAnnouncement.description: What a runner declares about its connection in `announce`.

concurrency_capacity.description: Maximum concurrent work this session accepts; it must be positive.

display_name.description:
Optional human-readable name shown to the owner; a supplied value is
non-blank and at most 128 bytes long.

handler_keys.description:
Stable handler keys the runner can execute. The set must contain 1 to
128 unique keys, each 1–128 bytes and matching
`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*`.

oneOf.description: Typed version of Tron's runner protocol understood by this session.

runner_version.description:
Optional runner implementation version, retained as display metadata;
a supplied value is non-blank and at most 128 bytes long.

sdk_version.description:
Optional semantic SDK version, used by the server to report whether
this session is older than a peer. A supplied value must parse as a
semantic version and be non-blank and at most 128 bytes long.

RunnerHandlerKey.description:
Stable, validated name of a runner handler.  Handler keys are durable job
configuration, rather than a free-form label inferred from live sessions.

`accept` must arrive by this time. It is the push time plus the
job's delivery timeout.

late.description:
True when the report arrived more than the job's lateness
threshold after the run's `scheduled_for`. A late report is
still recorded.

ServerMessage.description: Frames Tron sends to a runner.

worker_api_key.description: The connection itself carries no credential: no `Authorization` header and no organization header. Authentication happens inside the protocol. The first frame a runner sends must be `authenticate` carrying a worker API key token, created on the Runners page and shown once. Tron answers `authenticated` (with a fresh session id) or `authentication_failed` and then closes the connection. A first frame that does not arrive within 10 seconds, or is not a valid `authenticate`, is answered with `authentication_failed`.
